increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them test gaps rather than defects. What shipped: a collector-side lane join in store.getAgents behind GET /api/sessions/:id/agents, giving every span of a session a lane key of 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed' by resolving agent_id first and the parent-span chain second; a timeline module in argus-ui drawing one bar per lane over one shared window; and the six technical views (overview, todos, traces, events, metrics, raw) moved into a strip below the timeline, closed by default. npm --prefix tools/argus test 176 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 39 cases exit 0. Both correction rounds were spent because the visible behaviour was computed by a tested pure helper but never pinned in the rendered markup or the booted page; the round-2 fake-DOM harness in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs now boots public/app.js in-process, so later UI increments have a way to pin what the human sees.

increments.title: Activity and context growth drawn on each lane
increments.goal: Draw each lane's activity over time and, behind it, that agent's context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows its activity over time - tool calls and API requests - placed at the times they occurred, on the lane of the agent instance the activity belongs to.

Activity is assigned to lanes with the lane vocabulary the session's agents endpoint already serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed'), not a second attribution scheme; the records drawn here carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated.
Activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane rather than being dropped or folded into the main lane.
Each lane carries, as a curve or area behind that activity, the context size over time for that agent.

The curve is drawn from a size the telemetry actually records - the reported untruncated request-body length survives even when the body itself was truncated - and the view names which measure it is showing.
Growth in context size is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.
What proves this increment is the drawn result in the page: a change that stops the activity marks or the curve reaching the rendered timeline is caught, not only a computation checked in isolation.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: store.getAgents now joins claude_code.tool and claude_code.llm_request spans into a per-lane activity list and api_request_body records into a per-lane context series, both on the existing 'main' / 'agent:<agent_id>' / 'unattributed' lane keys; the content records carry no agent_id, so their lane is resolved through their spanId and a record whose span is unknown lands on unattributed, never on main; a requestBodyLength helper prefers the reported body_length over the delivered body, so a truncated or body_ref-only record still reports its true size; timeline.js draws an SVG area per lane scaled to one session-wide peak with activity ticks over it and a legend naming the measure; and app.test.mjs boots the real page and pins that marks and a non-empty polygon reach the rendered timeline. npm --prefix tools/argus test 186 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 54 cases exit 0. The fake-DOM harness plus the provability criterion cost this increment zero correction rounds, against two for the increment before it.

increments.title: Scrubbing the timeline, and a live mode that follows the head
increments.goal: Give the timeline a chosen time that can be moved to any point of the recorded session, plus a live mode that follows the newest data as it arrives.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session, and the chosen time is visible on the timeline.
The chosen time is drawn against the same shared window the lanes are already drawn against, so its position lines up with the activity marks and the context curve at that instant.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives, and keeps following as later data extends the session's window.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode.
A control returns to live mode.
The chosen time is one shared value the session view works from, so a later per-lane detail can be answered for exactly that moment.

What proves this increment is the behaviour of the page: a change that stops scrubbing moving the chosen time, or stops the live control returning to the head, is caught, not only a helper that maps a position to a time.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings on the first round. What shipped: state.atMs and state.following in app.js as the one chosen time the session view works from, chosenTimePct/clampChosenTime/laneRowsHtml/scrubStateHtml in timeline.js with a third options argument on timelineHtml, a playhead per lane placed by the same window arithmetic as the activity marks and the context curve, a range control that scrubs anywhere in the session, and a Live control that returns to the head; every refresh re-pins the chosen time to the head while following and only clamps a scrubbed time into the widened window. Two facts the next increment inherits: the scrub handler repaints the lanes and the readout in place through the ids timeline-lanes and timeline-scrub-state rather than re-rendering the detail, because a full render would destroy the range input mid-drag; and app.js's formatting helpers now live in public/format.js. npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 70 cases exit 0.

increments.title: Selecting a lane, and that agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Make a lane on the timeline selectable, and show for the selected lane the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each with its call parameters.
criteria: Selecting a lane on the timeline records a selection the session view holds beside the chosen time, and the selected lane is visibly marked on the timeline.
The lane selected is one of the lanes the timeline already draws, named by the lane vocabulary already in place (main, agent:<agent_id>, unattributed), not a second attribution scheme.
The selection shows the tools that agent has used up to the chosen time, each entry carrying the tool name and that call's parameters.

Whether the call parameters already arrive with the per-lane tool activity or have to be exposed for the first time is established and stated, and either way the panel reads them through the attribution already in place rather than joining records to agents a second way.

The listing is bounded by the selected lane and by the chosen time and follows the chosen time as it moves, so it never carries a call from after that moment; the scrub path repaints it in place, since a full re-render of the detail would destroy the range input mid-drag.

Which tools an agent used, and what for, is answerable for any lane the timeline draws at any point of the session, the unattributed lane included, and a lane with no tool calls before the chosen time says so.
With no lane selected the session view renders as it does today.

What proves this increment is the rendered page: a change that stops a lane selection reaching the panel, or leaves the panel showing the previous moment after the chosen time moves, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after one correction round, which was a test gap and not a defect. What shipped: state.selectedLaneId beside state.atMs, lane rows turned into selectable controls marked with aria-current, tool call parameters newly exposed on the span-derived per-lane activity entries of GET /api/sessions/:id/agents (joined from the tool_result log through tool_use_id in the existing single logs walk, capped at 1000 characters because that payload is refetched on every ingest tick), and a #lane-detail panel listing the selected lane's tool calls with parameters up to the chosen time, repainted in place by renderLaneDetail from both renderDetail and the scrub path so the range input survives a drag. npm --prefix tools/argus test 192 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 90 cases exit 0. The correction round went on the same trap as timeline-landing's: the fake DOM conjures an element for any id, so panel assertions that read only that element stayed green when the container was deleted from the rendered markup; the fix asserts the composed detail markup, and a mutation check proved 8 of 23 cases now fail when the container is removed.

increments.title: The selected lane context at the chosen time as a structured message list
increments.goal: Show, in the lane detail panel the selection already opens, the selected agent or main session context as of the chosen time, rendered as a message list whose blocks collapse to one line with a size and expand to the exact full text.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent - or the main session - context as of that moment, in the same lane detail panel the selection already opens, beside the tool listing that is already there.

The context shown is the body of the nearest API request at or before the chosen time on the selected lane, resolved through the lane attribution already in place; the body records carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated rather than joined a second way.
It is rendered as a structured message list distinguishing system prompt, user, assistant, tool call and tool result blocks.
Each block is collapsed to one line carrying its size, and expands to the exact full text the record carries.
A body the CLI truncated is marked as truncated instead of being presented as the whole context, and the size shown is the reported untruncated length rather than the delivered length.
A record that reports a body length but carries no body text at all is shown as its reported size with the text stated to be absent, rather than as an empty context.
A lane with no API request at or before the chosen time says so, rather than showing another lane context or the nearest later one.

Moving the chosen time moves the context shown, and the context and the tool listing agree about lane and time bound at every moment; the context joins the same in-place repaint path the tool listing already uses, so a scrub drag is not interrupted.

Where the full body text is fetched from is established and stated: the per-lane payload the page refetches on every ingest tick caps its inline text at a thousand characters for exactly this size reason, so the context body must not inflate that payload.

What proves this increment is the rendered page: the assertions read the composed session markup and not only an element the fake DOM conjures by id, so a change that stops the context reaching the panel, or stops an expanded block showing the full text, is caught.
increments.note: Kept as one increment and kept last, with its criteria sharpened by what lane-select showed. Four facts it now inherits instead of rediscovering: the panel, its container id and its in-place repaint from both the render path and the scrub path already exist, so this increment adds content to a panel rather than building one; body records are attributed to a lane through their span, which lane-activity already does for the context curve, so the nearest-request lookup has an attribution to reuse; the per-lane payload caps inline text at a thousand characters because it is refetched on every ingest tick, which is why the criteria now ask where the full body text is fetched from instead of assuming it rides along; and both UI increments that lost a correction round lost it to the same trap, a fake DOM that conjures an element for any id, so the proof criterion now names the composed markup explicitly. Nothing was split off: the collapsed line with its size and the expansion to full text are one deliverable, and half of it - a list of blocks nobody can open - is not worth a review of its own. This is the last open increment, so the run ends with it and the whole ./test.sh belongs in its final report; lane-select changed the collector but ran only the UI suite, and that gap should not repeat.

return.summary: Add a lane-scoped context route to the collector and a structured, collapsible message list to the lane detail panel, fetched per selection and chosen time so the 60 KB body never rides in the per-ingest lanes payload.
return.plan:
GOAL The lane detail panel that lane-select already opens gains a second section: the selected lane's context as of the chosen time, as a structured message list whose blocks collapse to one line with a size and expand to the exact full text. WHERE THE BODY TEXT COMES FROM (the load-bearing decision) `GET /api/sessions/:id/agents` is refetched on every coalesced ingest tick while a session is live; that is why `MAX_ACTIVITY_PARAMS_CHARS = 1000` (tools/argus/src/store.mjs:61) caps each tool call's parameters in it. A request body is routinely ~60 KB, so it must not ride in that payload. The body is fetched instead from a new, lane-scoped route that is called once per (lane, chosen time), not per ingest tick: GET /api/sessions/:id/context?lane=&at= COLLECTOR (tools/argus) 1. store.mjs — extract the lane attribution `getAgents` already has into a module-level helper so nothing joins a body to a lane a second way: function laneResolver(spans) { const byId = new Map(spans.map((s) => [s.spanId, s])); const laneKeys = new Map(); const laneKeyOf = (span, depth = 0) => { /* the body of the current getAgents laneKeyOf, unchanged */ }; /** The lane of a log record. These records carry no agent_id at all, so * their lane is the lane of the span they were emitted under; one that * names no span in the buffer is honestly unattributed. */ const laneOfLog = (log) => { const span = log.spanId ? byId.get(log.spanId) : null; return span ? laneKeyOf(span) : UNATTRIBUTED_LANE_ID; }; return { byId, laneKeyOf, laneOfLog }; } `getAgents` keeps its behaviour exactly: it now builds `const { byId, laneKeyOf, laneOfLog } = laneResolver(spans)` instead of its inline map/closure, its span loop still calls `laneFor(laneKeyOf(span))`, and its context walk becomes `laneFor(laneOfLog(log))`. Move the existing explanatory comments onto the helper rather than dropping them. 2. store.mjs — new method next to `getAgents`: getLaneContext(sessionId, laneId, atMs = null) Returns `null` for an unknown session (the same contract `getAgents` and `getSession` have). Otherwise `{ sessionId, laneId, atMs, record }` where `record` is `null` or: `{ seq, timeMs, spanId, traceId, length, truncated, text, ref, model, requestId }`. Selection rule, documented in the method's doc comment: over `this.logs`, keep every record of this session with `eventName === EVENT.apiRequestBody`, `timeMs > 0`, `timeMs <= atMs` (no upper bound when `atMs` is null), `requestBodyLength(log) !== null`, and `laneOfLog(log) === laneId`; answer the one with the greatest `timeMs`, ties resolved by the greater `seq`. Scan all of them — do not break at the first hit walking backwards, because arrival order is not time order (the reason `getAgents` sorts its samples). The predicate is `requestBodyLength`, not `contentOf`, on purpose and with a comment saying so: `contentOf` returns null for a record that carries neither text nor a `body_ref`, and such a record still reports `body_length` and is still drawn on the curve, so the panel must be able to show it as "this much context, text absent". Using `contentOf` here would silently show the previous request instead. Field derivation: `length = requestBodyLength(log)`; `const content = contentOf(log)`; `text = content?.text ?? null`; `ref = content?.ref ?? null`; `truncated = content ? content.truncated : bool(log.attrs?.body_truncated)`; `model = attrs.model ?? null`; `requestId = attrs.request_id ?? null`. No cap on `text` — the exact full text is the point, and this route is not on the per-tick path. 3. server.mjs — a route beside the `agentsMatch` one: const contextMatch = pathname.match(/^\/api\/sessions\/([^/]+)\/context$/); `lane` missing or empty -> 400 `{ error: 'lane required' }`; `store.getLaneContext(decodeURIComponent(id), lane, intParam(searchParams, 'at', null))` null -> 404 `{ error: 'unknown session' }`; otherwise 200 with the object. Note in a comment that this route answers with the whole body text on purpose, and that this is why the lanes payload does not. 4. README.md (tools/argus) — one row in the HTTP API table for the new route, and extend the existing "The lanes payload caps each tool call's parameters at 1000 characters" bullet under Limits to say that the request body is not in that payload either and is fetched per lane and moment through the new route. 5. scripts/demo-emit.mjs — today every emitted `api_request_body` carries a truncated JSON fragment, so a demo session would only ever exercise the raw/truncated path and never show a structured list. Make the main session's first request body per interaction a whole, parseable body (system string, a user message, an assistant message with a `tool_use` part, a user message with a `tool_result` part) with a matching `body_length` and no `body_truncated`, and leave the rest as they are so both paths stay visible. Small, untested, and the only way a human can eyeball this increment. INTERFACE (tools/argus-ui) 6. New module `public/context.js`, pure like `timeline.js` — touches no `document`, `window` or `location`: export function contextBlocks(text) -> [{ kind, label, text, length }] export function contextSectionHtml(context, laneId, atMs) -> string `contextBlocks` parses the request body text as JSON and maps it to blocks in order: - `body.system`: a string becomes one `{kind:'system', label:'system prompt'}`; an array becomes one block per element, using `element.text` when it is a string and `JSON.stringify(element)` otherwise. - `body.messages[]`: `content` as a string becomes one block of kind `user`/`assistant` (anything that is not `assistant` counts as `user`, labelled with the role as given). `content` as an array maps per part `type`: `text` -> the message's own kind; `thinking` -> `{kind:'assistant', label:'thinking', text: part.thinking ?? ''}`; `redacted_thinking` -> `{kind:'assistant', label:'redacted thinking', text: part.data ?? ''}`; `tool_use` -> `{kind:'tool_call', label: part.name ?? 'tool', text: JSON.stringify(part.input ?? null, null, 2)}`; `tool_result` -> `{kind:'tool_result', label: part.tool_use_id ?? 'tool result', text: }`; anything else -> `{kind: , label: part.type ?? 'part', text: JSON.stringify(part)}`. - `body.tools` (the tool definitions) is deliberately not rendered; it is configuration, not conversation. - `JSON.parse` throwing, a non-object result, or a result that yields no block at all (which is what a CLI-truncated body looks like) answers `[{kind:'raw', label:'body', text, length: text.length}]`. - Every block carries `length === block.text.length`. `contextSectionHtml(context, laneId, atMs)` renders the section and owns the agreement rule: when `context` is missing, or `context.laneId !== laneId`, or `context.atMs !== atMs`, it renders the pending state — never another lane's or another moment's body. States, each on the section container as `data-context-state`: `loading`, `error`, `none` (loaded, no record), `absent` (a record with `text === null`), `ready`. The container also carries `data-lane-context=""`, and in the loaded states `data-context-length=""` — the reported untruncated length, never `text.length`. A truncated record additionally carries `data-context-truncated="true"` and says in words that the CLI cut it, and may state how much arrived as long as the size it presents is the reported one. The `absent` state states that the record carries no body text and names `record.ref` (escaped) when there is one. The `none` state says no API request was made on this lane at or before the chosen time, worded distinctly from the tool listing's "No tool calls were made…". Times come from `fmtClock`, sizes from `fmtNum`, everything user-supplied through `esc`. Each block renders as native disclosure, so no click handler and no real DOM are needed to reach the full text:
…label… …fmtNum(length) chars… 
…esc(exact full text)…
Two hard constraints on this markup: it must never contain the literal substring `tool-call` (existing tests assert its absence in panels that have no tool calls — use `tool_call` with an underscore in the data attribute and `ctx-block*` class names), and no file under tools/argus-ui may contain the literal path of the collector project (the independence test forbids it), so comments say "the collector" instead. 7. `public/timeline.js` — `laneDetailHtml(items, atMs, selectedLaneId, context)` takes the context state as a fourth argument and renders `contextSectionHtml(context, lane.id, atMs)` inside the existing `data-lane-detail` panel, beside the tool listing (wrap both in a `lane-detail-body` element; the context section first, the tool listing second). Called with three arguments it still renders the panel, with the context section in its `loading` state. Import from `./context.js`. 8. `public/app.js`: - `state.laneContext = null`, shaped `{ laneId, atMs, status: 'ready'|'error', record }`. Reset it to null wherever `state.selectedLaneId` is reset (both `loadSession` paths and `selectSession`). - `renderLaneDetail()` passes `state.laneContext` as the fourth argument, and then calls `ensureLaneContext()`. - `ensureLaneContext()` returns a promise and does nothing when there is no session, no selection, `state.atMs === null`, the selected lane is not among `state.agents`, the cached entry already matches `(state.selectedLaneId, state.atMs)`, or a request for that same key is already scheduled or in flight. Otherwise it schedules, after `CONTEXT_FETCH_DELAY_MS = 120`, a fetch of `/api/sessions//context` with `{ lane, at }` through the existing `api()` helper. The delay exists because a scrub drag fires `input` continuously and every answer can be tens of kilobytes. - When the answer lands: drop it if `(state.selectedLaneId, state.atMs)` has moved on; otherwise store `{laneId, atMs, status:'ready', record: payload?.record ?? null}` and call `renderLaneDetail()`. A failed fetch stores `{…, status:'error', record:null}` for the same key, so the page says so once instead of retrying forever; the next chosen time is a new key and retries by itself. - Nothing else changes: the panel keeps being repainted in place by `renderChosenTime()`, so a scrub drag still never touches the range input. 9. `public/styles.css` — lay the panel body out as two columns on wide screens (context, tool listing) and one column when narrow; style `details.ctx-block` so the collapsed summary is one line with the size at its end, and the expanded `
` wraps and scrolls rather than stretching the page. Give each `data-block-kind` a distinguishable accent.

10. `README.md` (tools/argus-ui) — extend the Timeline bullet: the selection also shows that lane's context as of the chosen time as a structured, expandable message list, fetched per lane and moment.

WHAT WAS REJECTED
- Carrying the body text in the `/agents` payload: that payload is refetched on every ingest tick and already caps inline text at 1000 characters for exactly this reason.
- Adding a `lane` filter to `/api/content` instead of a new route: `contentOf` drops a record that reports `body_length` but carries neither text nor reference, and that record is precisely the one criterion 6 requires to be shown; the lookup has to use the same `requestBodyLength` predicate the curve uses.
- Resolving "nearest at or before" in the browser from `lane.context`: that array is thinned to 1000 samples by peak, so its nearest sample is not always the nearest record, and it carries no text anyway.
- Parsing the message list in the collector: the collector serves records as recorded, and the message shape is a rendering concern the interface's pure layer can pin without a DOM.
- A JavaScript expand/collapse handler: `
/` needs no listener and puts the full text in the markup, where a test can read it.
- Showing the last loaded body while a newer one is in flight: the context and the tool listing must agree about lane and bound at every moment, so a mismatch renders the pending line naming the current bound instead.
- Re-rendering the whole detail pane when the fetch lands: that would replace the range input mid-drag, which is the one thing `renderChosenTime` exists to prevent.

return.environment:
Node v22.22.2 is installed; both projects declare `engines.node >= 20.11`, have zero runtime dependencies and no build step, so nothing needs installing and `npm install` is never run.
There is no linter and no formatter in this repository — no lint command exists to run.
Test commands used by this plan, all from the repository root:
- `npm --prefix tools/argus test` — the collector suite (`node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`).
- `npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` — the interface suite (same runner).
- `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs` — one file at a time.
- `./test.sh` — every suite in the repository; needs bash and git (it runs `test-repo.sh` and `test-worktree.sh`, which creates git worktrees) and is the command the issue's last acceptance criterion names.
HTTP tests bind port 0 and ask the OS which port they got; no fixed port is required and no collector needs to be running.
return.testPlan:
WHETHER: tests are needed, at three levels — the collector's new lookup and route, the interface's new pure module, and the rendered page. Nothing was run to write this plan: no suite, no baseline. The tree is expected green before the new cases land (lane-select closed with an accepted review), and the new cases are expected red until the implementation exists. The first run belongs to whoever runs it downstream. GENERAL CONVENTIONS (all four files): `node:test` with `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, ESM `.mjs`, no dependencies, no mocking library. Test names are lowercase sentences stating the rule the case fixes. Comments above a case explain why the case exists, never what the code does. === A. /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs (unit) === Add one section, `/* --------------- getLaneContext --------------- */`, after the existing getAgents sections. Use the file's own helpers: `SESSION = 'sess-1'`, `NOW`, `log(eventName, attrs, timeMs)`, `span(name, attrs, extra)`, `subagentSpan(name, agentId, extraAttrs, extra)`. A log is given a span the way the file already does it: `{ ...log('claude_code.api_request_body', {...}, NOW + 50), spanId: 'llm-a' }`. Each case builds its own `new TelemetryStore()` and calls `store.ingest('traces', [...])` then `store.ingest('logs', [...])`. Run this file with `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`. A1 — nearest at or before, on the selected lane. Spans: `span('claude_code.interaction', {}, { spanId: 'root' })` and `subagentSpan('claude_code.llm_request', 'agt-a', {}, { spanId: 'llm-a', parentSpanId: 'root' })`. Logs: three `api_request_body` under `llm-a` at NOW+10/+20/+30 with distinct `body` strings and `body_length`, plus one under `root` at NOW+25. `store.getLaneContext(SESSION, 'agent:agt-a', NOW + 25)` answers `record.timeMs === NOW + 20` and `record.text` equal to that body — not the main lane's at +25, not the later one at +30. Proves criteria 2 and 7. A2 — nothing before the bound. Same fixture, bound NOW+5: the answer is an object whose `record` is null and whose `sessionId`/`laneId`/`atMs` echo the query. Proves criterion 7. A3 — unknown session. `assert.equal(store.getLaneContext('nope', 'main', NOW), null)`. A4 — the main session's own context. A body under a span with no agent attributes and no parent resolves to lane `main`, and `getLaneContext(SESSION, 'agent:agt-a', …).record` is null for it. Proves criterion 1 for the main lane. A5 — a body naming no span. Loop `for (const spanId of ['gone', ''])` like the existing unattributed case: the record answers on `unattributed` and not on `main`. Proves criterion 2's attribution rule end to end. A6 — truncation. Attrs `{ body: '{"m":1}', body_truncated: 'true', body_length: '120000' }`: `record.length === 120000`, `record.truncated === true`, `record.text === '{"m":1}'`. Proves criterion 5 at the source. A7 — a reported length with no text at all. Attrs `{ body_length: '900' }` only: the record is answered with `length === 900`, `text === null`, `ref === null`. In the same case assert the deliberate contrast — `store.queryContent({ sessionId: SESSION, kinds: ['request_body'] })` returns `[]` for that record — with a comment that the content list cannot serve it while the curve counts it, which is why this lookup does not use the same predicate. Proves criterion 6 at the source. A8 — a file reference. Attrs `{ body_ref: '/tmp/body.json', body_length: '5000' }`: `record.ref === '/tmp/body.json'`, `record.text === null`, `record.length === 5000`. A9 — out-of-order arrival. Ingest the logs in the order +30, +10, +20 (one `store.ingest('logs', […])` in that order): the answer at bound NOW+25 is still the +20 record. Pins that the scan does not stop at the first backwards hit. A10 — only request bodies. An `api_response_body` at NOW+30 and a `user_prompt` at NOW+20 under the same span as an `api_request_body` at NOW+10: the answer at NOW+40 is the request at NOW+10. Edges left untested here and why: eviction and retention (unchanged buffers, already covered), and a `laneId` naming a lane that never existed (answers the same `record: null` as A2 by construction, so a second case buys nothing). === B. /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs (integration over HTTP) === Add cases after the existing agent-lane route cases. Conventions: `await withServer({}, async ({ base }) => { … })`, ingest through real requests to `${base}/v1/traces` with `agentsTracePayload(sessionId)` (root span id `'22'.repeat(8)`, agt-a tool span `'33'.repeat(8)`, agt-b tool span `'44'.repeat(8)`) and to `${base}/v1/logs` with `contentLogsPayloadJson(sessionId, [{ eventName, timeMs, spanId, attrs }])`; assert the ingest status first, as the file already does, so a failed POST reports as itself. Run with `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`. B1 — the context reaches a client, and the lanes payload stays free of it. Ingest the agents trace plus one `claude_code.api_request_body` under the agt-a tool span whose `attrs.body` is a whole parseable request body (a recognisable marker string inside it, e.g. a user message reading `needle-in-the-body`) and whose `body_length` is larger than the delivered text. Then: `GET /api/sessions/:id/agents` is 200 and `JSON.stringify(payload)` does not contain `needle-in-the-body`, while `lane.context[0].length` is the reported length; `GET /api/sessions/:id/context?lane=agent:agt-a&at=` is 200 and `record.text` equals the ingested body string exactly, with `record.length` the reported one. This single case carries criterion 9. B2 — unknown session. `GET /api/sessions/nope/context?lane=main` is 404 with `{ error: 'unknown session' }`. B3 — no lane named. `GET /api/sessions/:id/context` (no `lane`) is 400. B4 — a lane with nothing before the bound. `GET /api/sessions/:id/context?lane=agent:agt-b&at=` is 200 with `record === null`. Left untested: token auth on the new route (it sits behind the same blanket `/api/` gate every other route uses, already covered) and persistence replay (the route reads the same store the ingest fills). === C. /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs (NEW, unit) === A new file for the new module, matching the project's one-test-file-per-module habit. Header comment: this pins the pure half of the context view — no `document`, no fetch. Imports: `import { contextBlocks, contextSectionHtml } from '../public/context.js';`. Two local helpers at the top of the file, in the style of `timeline.test.mjs`'s `lane({...})`: /** A record shaped like one `record` of the collector's /context answer. */ function record(over = {}) { return { seq: 1, timeMs: 1_000, spanId: 'llm-a', traceId: 't', length: 0, truncated: false, text: null, ref: null, model: 'claude-opus-5', requestId: 'req_1', ...over }; } /** The loaded context state the page holds for one lane at one moment. */ const loaded = (rec, laneId = 'main', atMs = 2_000) => ({ laneId, atMs, status: 'ready', record: rec }); Run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs`. C1 — the five block kinds. `contextBlocks(JSON.stringify({ system: 'You are a researcher.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'find the needle' }, { role: 'assistant', content: [ { type: 'text', text: 'searching' }, { type: 'tool_use', name: 'Grep', input: { pattern: 'needle' } } ] }, { role: 'user', content: [ { type: 'tool_result', tool_use_id: 'tu_1', content: '42 hits' } ] } ] }))` yields blocks whose `kind`s are `['system','user','assistant','tool_call','tool_result']` in that order; the tool_call block's text contains `pattern` and `needle`; the tool_result block's text is `42 hits`; every block satisfies `block.length === block.text.length`. Proves criterion 3. C2 — a truncated body. `contextBlocks('{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"…')` yields exactly one block of kind `raw` whose text is the input, unchanged. Also assert an empty string and a body that parses to a number both yield one `raw` block rather than throwing. C3 — the reported size wins. `contextSectionHtml(loaded(record({ text: '{"m":1}', length: 120_000, truncated: true })), 'main', 2_000)` contains `data-context-state="ready"`, `data-context-truncated="true"` and `data-context-length="120000"`, and does not present `7` as the size. Proves criterion 5. C4 — text absent. `loaded(record({ text: null, length: 900 }))` gives `data-context-state="absent"`, `data-context-length="900"`, matches `/no body text/i`, and contains no `` tag has no ` open` attribute, and the rendered `
` contains all 3000 characters. Proves criterion 4.
C10 — escaping. A user message text of `` and a `tool_use` named ``: the html contains no `` (platform behaviour), and CSS.

=== D. /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs (unit) ===
Two cases in the existing lane-detail section, using the file's `lane({...})` fixture helper and direct calls to `laneDetailHtml`. Run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`.
D1 — the panel holds both sections. `laneDetailHtml([l], 500, 'main', { laneId: 'main', atMs: 500, status: 'ready', record: { …a small parseable body, length matching… } })` where `l` has one tool call at atMs 100: the html contains `data-lane-detail="main"`, `data-lane-context="main"`, at least one `data-block-kind=`, and the tool call's name, and the `data-lane-detail` opening tag comes before both. Proves criterion 1's "same panel, beside the tool listing".
D2 — three-argument calls still work. `laneDetailHtml([l], 500, 'main')` renders the tool listing unchanged and the context section in `data-context-state="loading"`.

=== E. /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs (the rendered page — criterion 10) ===
This file boots the real `public/app.js` against the fake DOM. Extend it, do not restructure it.

Fixture work, once, near `agentsOne`:
- A `laneBodies` map, oldest first per lane, matching the times already in `agentsOne.context`: `main` gets two entries — at `T0 + 500` a body of `{ system: 'You are the main session.', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'read the early file' }] }` with `length` 20000, and at `T0 + 8_000` a body that additionally carries an assistant message with a `tool_use` part naming `Write` with input `{ file_path: '/late.md' }` and a user message with a `tool_result` part reading `wrote 12 lines`, with `length` 90000; `agent:agt-a` gets one entry at `T0 + 1_500` with `truncated: true`, `length: 65_000` and the unparseable text `'{"model":"m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"…'`; `unattributed` gets one at `T0 + 6_500` with `text: null` and `length: 900`; `agent:agt-b` gets none.
- A `'/api/sessions/sess-1/context'` entry in `baseRoutes`, written as a function of the url so the page's own query is what selects the answer: read `url.searchParams.get('lane')` and `Number(url.searchParams.get('at'))`, keep the entries of that lane with `timeMs <= at`, and answer `{ sessionId: 'sess-1', laneId: lane, atMs: at, record:  }`. Put it in `baseRoutes` rather than in single tests so the existing lane-select cases keep getting a sane answer instead of the 404 branch.
- In `installFakes`, push the whole `url` into a new `urls` array beside the existing `paths.push(url.pathname)` and return `urls` on the handle; E7 needs the query string.

Because an in-place repaint writes only into the `lane-detail` element, and the fake DOM does not reflect that back into `detail.innerHTML`, the composed-markup assertions are made after the next wholesale render: select, settle on `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML`, then `handle.emit('ingest')` and settle until `laneDetailSlice(handle.el('detail').innerHTML)` carries the state you are about to assert. Write that reason as a comment once. The `baseRoutes` `/agents` fixture is a constant object, so the ingest does not move `atMs` and the loaded context still matches. Run this file with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs`.

E1 — the context reaches the composed panel, beside the tool listing. Boot with `baseRoutes`, `handle.fire('detail', 'click', clickOn('[data-lane-id]', { dataset: { laneId: 'main' } }))`, settle until the panel element contains `data-context-state="ready"`, emit an ingest, settle until `laneDetailSlice(handle.el('detail').innerHTML)` contains `data-context-state="ready"`. On that slice assert: `data-lane-context="main"`, `data-block-kind="system"`, `data-block-kind="user"`, `data-block-kind="tool_call"`, `data-block-kind="tool_result"`, and the tool listing's `/late.md` — one panel carrying both. Also `assert.ok(handle.paths.includes('/api/sessions/sess-1/context'))`. Proves criteria 1, 3 and 10.
E2 — an expanded block carries the exact full text. On the same composed slice, take the fixture's user message string (`read the early file`) from the fixture rather than retyping it, and assert the slice contains `data-block-size="${text.length}"` and a `
` whose content includes that exact string. Proves criterion 4 on the page.
E3 — moving the chosen time moves the context, in place. Select `main`, settle on ready, then `handle.fire('detail', 'input', { target: { id: 'timeline-scrub', value: String(T0 + 5_000) } })` and settle until `handle.el('lane-detail').innerHTML` no longer contains `data-block-kind="tool_call"` (the +8 000 body is gone) while still containing `data-context-state="ready"`. In the same panel assert the tool listing shows `/early.md` and not `/late.md` — context and listing agree on the bound. Assert `handle.el('detail').innerHTML` still contains `value="${T0 + 10_000}"`, which is how this file already pins that the wholesale render did not run and the range input survived. Then scrub to `T0 + 9_500` and settle until the `tool_call` block is back. Proves criterion 8.
E4 — a lane with no request says so. Select `agent:agt-b`, settle on `data-context-state="none"`, emit an ingest, and assert on the composed slice: matches `/no api request/i`, contains no `data-block-kind=`, and contains none of main's texts (`read the early file`). Proves criterion 7 on the page.
E5 — a truncated body is marked. Select `agent:agt-a`, settle, ingest, and assert the composed slice carries `data-context-truncated="true"` and `data-context-length="65000"`. Proves criterion 5 on the page.
E6 — a reported size with no text. Select `unattributed`, settle, ingest, and assert the composed slice carries `data-context-state="absent"`, `data-context-length="900"`, matches `/no body text/i` and contains no `data-block-kind=`. Proves criterion 6 on the page.
E7 — the page asks for the selected lane at the chosen time. After selecting `agent:agt-a` and settling, find the recorded url whose pathname ends in `/context` and assert `searchParams.get('lane') === 'agent:agt-a'` and `Number(searchParams.get('at')) === T0 + 10_000`. Proves criterion 2's "resolved through the lane attribution" from the client side.
Existing cases in this file must keep passing untouched; the new markup must never contain the substring `tool-call`, which several of them assert the absence of.

WHAT IS LEFT UNTESTED ON PURPOSE
- `styles.css`: nothing in this repository asserts CSS, and "beside" is a layout decision.
- The 120 ms debounce interval: a timing assertion would be flaky; what is pinned is that the panel arrives, through `settle`.
- `scripts/demo-emit.mjs`: the script has no test file and no suite runs it.
- README wording in either project.
- Native `
` toggling in a browser: the markup carrying the full text is what is asserted.

increments.title: The selected agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, the tools that agent has used up to that moment together with the parameters of each call.
increments.note: Dropped as its own increment and never revived under this id. Its criteria were folded into context-at-time after content-pipeline showed tool parameters arrive as the same content records as request bodies and lane-activity put each lane tool calls, with names and times, on the /agents payload; after scrub-live they moved on into lane-select, which now carries the selection plus the tool listing while context-at-time carries the context. The work happens, under those two ids.

return.summary: Closed lane-select as done (review accepted, one correction round spent on a test gap, not a defect) and left one increment open, context-at-time, sharpened rather than re-cut. Six of the issue's ten acceptance criteria are delivered and closed; the structured-message-list criterion is the only one still open, and context-at-time carries it whole. No split: the collapsed line with its size and the expansion to the exact text are one deliverable, and a list of blocks nobody can open is not worth its own review chain. Four facts from lane-select changed its criteria: the lane detail panel, its container and its in-place repaint from both the render path and the scrub path already exist, so this increment adds content to an existing panel; body records are attributed to a lane through their span, which lane-activity already does for the context curve, so the nearest-request lookup reuses that attribution instead of inventing one; the per-lane payload caps inline text at a thousand characters because it is refetched on every ingest tick, so a new criterion asks where the full body text is fetched from instead of letting it ride along on that payload; and both UI increments that lost a correction round lost it to a fake DOM that conjures an element for any id, so the proof criterion now names the composed session markup explicitly. Three of at most eight increments remain unspent, which leaves room to re-cut if the request-body shape turns out worse than expected.
